Incident Type: FIXED

Medium Affected: AIR
Suspected Responsible Party: BP AMERICA PRODUCTION CO.
Skytruth Analysis
ON 12/24/2005 THE WATTENBERG GAS PLANT RECEIVED LARGE VOLUMES OF SLUG HYDROCARBON LIQUIDS IN OUR INLET GAS PIPELINE FEEDING THE PLANT. THE LARGE VOLUME OF SLUG HYDROCARBON LIQUIDS WAS A RESULT OF KERR MCGEES PIPELINE PIGGING OPERATIONS ON THEIR PIPELINE FIELD GATHERING SYSTEMS. KERR MCGEE TRANSPORTS GAS TO THE WATTENBERG GAS PLANT FOR PROCESSING.AT THE SAME TIME WE WERE RECEIVING ABNORMALLY LARGE VOLUMES OF SLUG HYDROCARBON LIQUIDS THE PLANT OPERATIONS GROUP HAD TO SWITCH PRODUCT TREATER BEDS AS PART OF NORMAL OPERATING PROCEDURES. DURING THE SWITCHING PROCESS PRODUCT TREATER BED HAS TO VENT TO THE C4+ TANK WHERE THE SLUG LIQUIDS ARE STORED. WITH THE UNUSALLY HIGH VOLUME OF SLUG HYDROCARBON LIQUIDS AND THE VENTING OF THE PRODUCT TREATER BEDS AT THE SAME TIME RESULTED IN OUR HAVING TO VENT GAS FROM OUR C4+ STORAGE TANK TO THE PLANT FLARE STACK.THE VENTING OF GAS OCCURRED FROM 6:30 AM UNTIL 2:00PM AND A TOTAL OF 10.5 LBS OF NOX EMISSIONS TO THE ATMOSPHEREFROM THE FLARE.

properties.summary: Incident Type: VESSEL - NRC Report ID: 1030755 - Medium Affected: WATER - Suspected Responsible Party: VIGOR MARINE LLC
properties.content:
Report Details
NRC Report ID: 1030755
Incident Time: 2012-11-15 13:05:00
Nearest City: Portland, OR
Location: MV CAPE HUDSON AND ADJACENT BERTH 312 5555 N CHANNEL AVENUE
Incident Type: VESSEL
Material: CASTROL AWH M68
Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party: VIGOR MARINE LLC
SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 45.565000, -122.726667 (Explicit)
Reported Spill Volume: 10 gallons
Report Description
***WEB REPORT*** MV CAPE HUDSON WAS AT BERTH 312, VIGOR MARINE LLC UNDERGOING A REPAIR AVAILABILITY. VIGOR PERSONNEL REQUESTED THE ATTENDANCE OF SHIP’S CREW TO WITNESS OPERATIONAL TEST OF THE STBD AFT MIDSHIPS MOORING WINCH AFTER COMPLETION OF REPAIRS. THE HYDRAULIC SYSTEM FOR AFT WINCH AND ASSOCIATED STBD FWD MIDSHIP MOORING WINCH HAD VALVES AND CIRCUITS TAGGED OUT BY A VIGOR EMPLOYEE. A VIGOR EMPLOYEE REMOVED THE TAGS AND ADVISED SHIP’S CREW IT WAS OK TO OPERATE THE WINCH. WHEN THE SYSTEM WAS OPERATED THE FWD WINCH MOTOR CASING BLEW OUT DUE TO OVERPRESSURE CAUSED BY CLOSED VALVES. THE MAJORITY OF THE HYDRAULIC OIL WAS CONTAINED ON BOARD. SOME OIL SPRAYED ONTO THE ADJACENT BERTH 312. APPROXIMATELY ½ CUP OF OIL WENT INTO THE WILLAMETTE RIVER BETWEEN THE BERTH AND THE SHIP. NO OIL SHEEN WAS OBSERVED IN THE WATER. THE VESSEL HAS AN OIL BOOM AROUND IT. FURTHER INVESTIGATION INDICATED THAT THE VIGOR EMPLOYEE REMOVING THE TAGS WAS NOT THE EMPLOYEE WHO HAD PLACED THE TAGS ON THE HYDRAULIC SYSTEM, THE SHIP’S CREW WAS UNAWARE OF THIS.

Report Description
***WEB REPORT*** A TRACTOR TRAILER CAUGHT FIRE AT THE REST AREA OFF I-75 SOUTH NEAR MM 128 IN GEORGETOWN, KY. THE TRACTOR TRAILER FIRE CAUSED THE RELEASE OF DIESEL FUEL AND HYDRAULIC OIL ONTO AN AREA OF THE ASPHALT PARKING LOT MEASURING APPROXIMATELY 50' BY 150' AND TRAVELED ANOTHER 100' LONG WHERE IT IMPACTED A NEARBY STORM DRAIN. THE IMPACTED STORM DRAIN RELEASED INTO A SOIL DITCH/FIELD WHERE IT POOLED UP IN A 5' BY 10' AREA. AN ENVIRONMENTAL CONTRACTOR HAS BEEN DISPATCHED TO PERFORM CLEAN UP OPERATIONS. THE ENVIRONMENTAL CONTRACTOR WILL UTILIZE A VACUUM TRUCK TO COLLECT THE RELEASED MATERIAL FROM THE STORM DRAIN AND THE SOIL DITCH AND WILL APPLY, COLLECT AND CONTAINERIZE GRANULAR ABSORBENTS TO THE IMPACTED ASPHALT.

OIL/SALTWATER TRAVELED APPROXIMATELY 40-YARDS DOWNHILL INTO WHAT APPEARS TO BE AN EPHEMERAL STREAM. FROM POINT OF ENTRY, OIL/SALT WATER TRAVELED AN ADDITIONAL 30-40-YARDS BEFORE POOLING-UP. REPLACED BAD SECTION OF PIPE WITH 8’ STEEL SUB. BOOM IN PLACE TO PREVENT FURTHER MIGRATION OF OIL. YELLOW-DOG PUMP IN PLACE UTILIZING A MAKE-SHIFT OIL/WATER SEPARATOR TO RECOVER OIL.
